pending_commit.commit_message: tast: Introduce chromeos-base/tast-build-deps. This CL introduces the chromeos-base/tast-build-deps package where build time dependencies of all Tast related binaries (test runners and test bundles) are put. This package resolves a few problems about interaction between Portage and Tast: - Portage has a bug that --onlydeps-with-rdeps=n is ignored in a certain situation (https://bugs.gentoo.org/682472) and Tast had to work around the bug in a hacky and incomplete way when installing build time dependencies. The hack is no longer required after introduction of this package since the new package has no runtime-only dependency. - Formerly users were prompted to emerge dependencies even just after running update_chroot because local test dependencies were not installed to the host, adding tens of seconds to the runtime of the tast command. Now those dependencies are installed by update_chroot, so there is no need of additional emerge. BUG=chromium:940761 TEST=./update_chroot TEST=./build_packages --board=betty Cq-Depend: chrome-internal:1387678 Cq-Depend: chrome-internal:1387312 Change-Id: I9d48c1a2c87a8da8c3774b8a8e124934d7122656 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1660509 Tested-by: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org>

BACKPORT: VSOCK: use TCP state constants for sk_state There are two state fields: socket->state and sock->sk_state. The socket->state field uses SS_UNCONNECTED, SS_CONNECTED, etc while the sock->sk_state typically uses values that match TCP state constants (TCP_CLOSE, TCP_ESTABLISHED). AF_VSOCK does not follow this convention and instead uses SS_* constants for both fields. The sk_state field will be exposed to userspace through the vsock_diag interface for ss(8), netstat(8), and other programs. This patch switches sk_state to TCP state constants so that the meaning of this field is consistent with other address families. Not just AF_INET and AF_INET6 use the TCP constants, AF_UNIX and others do too. The following mapping was used to convert the code: SS_FREE -> TCP_CLOSE SS_UNCONNECTED -> TCP_CLOSE SS_CONNECTING -> TCP_SYN_SENT SS_CONNECTED -> TCP_ESTABLISHED SS_DISCONNECTING -> TCP_CLOSING VSOCK_SS_LISTEN -> TCP_LISTEN In __vsock_create() the sk_state initialization was dropped because sock_init_data() already initializes sk_state to TCP_CLOSE. Signed-off-by: Stefan Hajnoczi <stefanha@redhat.com> Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net> (cherry picked from commit 3b4477d2dcf2709d0be89e2a8dced3d0f4a017f2) Signed-off-by: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org> BUG=chromium:848063 TEST=while true; do curl localhost:8080; done Conflicts: net/vmw_vsock/hyperv_transport.c - does not exist in 4.4 Change-Id: Id1d0b90c8909170eb9a93f59fae2a9040de0131d Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1663063 Tested-by: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sonny Rao <sonnyrao@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: vsock/virtio: set SOCK_DONE on peer shutdown Set the SOCK_DONE flag to match the TCP_CLOSING state when a peer has shut down and there is nothing left to read. This fixes the following bug: 1) Peer sends SHUTDOWN(RDWR). 2) Socket enters TCP_CLOSING but SOCK_DONE is not set. 3) read() returns -ENOTCONN until close() is called, then returns 0. Signed-off-by: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: David S. tast: Remove -checktestdeps=auto flag value. -checktestdeps controls the behavior to skip tests by checking software dependencies. Formerly the flag had three values: always, never, auto. The auto value, which was actually the default when the flag is not explicitly specified, indicates that software deps should be checked if and only if tests are specified by attribute expressions (e.g. "(!disabled)") rather than exact names (e.g. "arc.Boot") or globs (e.g. "arc.*"). Since this behavior is confusing, this CL changes the flag to accept a boolean value, and sets the default to always checking software dependencies. Fortunately, there is no use of the flag in production today: http://cs/search/?q=%22-checktestdeps%22 BUG=chromium:971486 TEST=fast_build.sh -T TEST=fast_build.sh && ~/go/bin/tast run betty arc.Boot audio.DevicePlay Change-Id: I3edb2eaca0ccd84f5826eb75362000d482906c27 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1666817 Tested-by: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hidehiko Abe <hidehiko@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Keigo Oka <oka@chromium.org>

autotest: Relax /dev/kvm check Devices that have recently added kvm support will sometimes fail provisioning if they haven't been through a cold reboot. This isn't an issue for most boards, but for boards that get provisioned with images that sometimes have kvm support and sometimes do not the check for /dev/kvm will fail. Let's relax this check on boards that have the kvm_transition flag declared. tast-test: Fix test volumes creation and removal timing issues. DMVerity tests create temporary volumes. There are instances where the log shows some potential timing issues between the volume cleanup and the creation of the volume re-using the same name. Add the use of temporary volume names, so tests do not re-use the same volume name. Add '--force' and '--retry' when cleaning up volumes. Add status check after volume creation / removal to force a flush. BUG=chromium:976162 TEST=ran test on betty. monitor on VM that the test is creating temporary volumes and that those are removed. (ls /dev/mapper). send sig-kill to running test to leave volume and make sure the test re-run properly.
